To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The WfMC Workflow Reference Model is the most comprehensive workflow model available today.
the WfMC's Reference Model is a good basis for a standard, that the Wf-XML is an appropriate starting point for a standard, and that the WfMS vendors are ready to support the standard.
the current standards for workflow interoperability are not sufficient to enable a wide-spread use.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues:
* _Interoperability_ between different workflow management systems (WFMS).

the following questions: What are the requirements of workflow interoperability? What are the current efforts to standardize workflow? What are the advantages and disadvantages of each effort? What is the future of workflow interoperability?
the following issues: (1) The definition of the workflow interoperability problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WfMC is currently the most active organization working on a workflow standard.
the current efforts toward a workflow interoperability standard are not yet sufficient for the purpose of enabling the envisioned Internet-scale workflow.
the current state of standardization in the area of workflow interoperability is still far from being complete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a set of specifications that can be used to describe workflows and workflow processes, to exchange workflow information, and to control workflow engines.
we have a lot of standards and specifications, but not a single workflow interoperability standard.
we have developed a standard that can be implemented in a variety of ways and that can be extended to support a variety of applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
workflow interoperability standards should not be limited to the exchange of workflow definitions, but should be extended to cover the exchange of workflow instances and their execution.
the current standards do not address the needs of workflow systems that have to interoperate in a heterogeneous environment.
the Internet community is moving toward a common standard for workflow interoperablity.
